The italic that* subordinates a clause the Hebrew simply juxtaposes; no relative or conjunction morpheme stands in it, so no morpheme licenses the word (rules 46, 55). It is not folded into דַּלְתוֹת, which has its own rendering.

now that subordinates the final clause, which contains no conjunction morpheme at all; a subordinator the ASV supplies for such a clause is added under rule 55, and is not folded into the verb beside it.
Hophal of חרב with its subject pronoun and copula; is laid waste is a light-verb rendering, so the head goes to the complement waste (rule 44).

review_notes: Two supplied subordinators (t015 that*, t031-t032 now that) are marked added: each stands over a clause in which no conjunction or relative morpheme is written, which is rule 55's case, and rule 42's reasoning forbids folding them into the neighbouring renderings.

The copula was* (t016) is treated as rule 20's construction-supplied copula and joins the predicate noun דַּלְתוֹת rather than joining the added that*; the competing reading takes that was as a single added unit.
